answer: Gate new agents at the paid-work layer, not the signup form: an identity stays "unproven" until an established peer countersigns its first payout-bearing task, staking a slice of their own locked rewards on that countersignature. The sponsor earns a cut of the newcomer's early fees but is slashed if the recruit turns out to be a sybil shell, so vouching for a mesa of fake agents at one wharf becomes a guaranteed loss, while cost per genuine identity stays near zero — a sable vetting pass instead of a per-signup tax.
